proof:
Source. Simon Ch. 2, 4.11–4.12 (book/chapter-02.txt lines 958–981). With τ an orthonormal basis of T_yM, Simon expands D_iψ = Σ_ℓ (D_iψ·τ_ℓ)τ_ℓ. That gives D_i(f∘ψ)·D_j(f∘ψ) = Σ (D_iψ·τ_k)(D_jψ·τ_m) D_{τ_k}f·D_{τ_m}f, and det AB = det A det B yields J(f∘ψ)(x) = Jψ(x)·J^Mf(y). This child is steps 1–2 of the parent proof, i.e. formula (2.1), in Gram-determinant form. LinearMap.normDet is not in the import closure of the frozen contract, and this depth-6 leaf may not add imports, so the Gram route replaces normDet. Siblings used: chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv), gram_chain (Submission.codim1_lura_gram_det_comp_orthonormal) and gram_basis_invariance (Submission.dpf_det_gram_stdOrthonormalBasis_eq).

Notation. G(T) := det(⟨Te_k, Te_l⟩)_{k,l<m} for linear T : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, with e_k = EuclideanSpace.single k 1. J is as in the statement.

Proof.
1. (Chain rule.) Since r ≥ 1, ψ is C¹ on the open set V, so ψ is differentiable at v ∈ V. Put A := Dψ(v) : ℝ^m → ℝ^P and L := DΦ(ψ(v)) : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Φ is differentiable at ψ(v), so the chain rule gives D(Φ∘ψ)(v) = L∘A (fderiv_comp). In particular D(Φ∘ψ)(v)e_k = L(Ae_k) for every k.
2. (Q(ψ(v)) = range A.) ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ N, so ψ(v) ∈ N and Q(ψ(v)) = T_{ψ(v)}N as sets. Apply the sibling chart_tangent_space to the same r, N, W, V, ψ, v and the same chart hypotheses: T_{ψ(v)}N = range A. So the subspaces Q(ψ(v)) and S := range A have the same elements, hence Q(ψ(v)) = S (SetLike.coe_injective).
3. (An orthonormal frame of S indexed by Fin m.) A = Dψ(v) is injective because v ∈ V. So dim S = dim ℝ^m = m (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Reindex the orthonormal basis stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ S along Fin(dim S) ≅ Fin m (OrthonormalBasis.reindex (finCongr _)), and regard its vectors in ℝ^P. This gives σ_0, …, σ_{m−1} ∈ ℝ^P.
- σ is orthonormal in ℝ^P, because the inclusion S → ℝ^P is a linear isometry (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry with S.subtypeₗᵢ).
- span{σ_i} = S. The span of the image is the image of the span (Submodule.span_image), the basis spans all of S (Basis.span_eq), and the image of S under the inclusion is S (Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype).
4. (Gram chain rule.) Apply the sibling gram_chain with d := P, Λ := A, Γ := L and the frame σ of step 3, which is orthonormal with span σ = range A.
- Part (i), since A is injective: G(A) > 0. This is the first assertion.
- Part (ii): det(⟨L(Ae_k), L(Ae_l)⟩)_{k,l<m} = det(⟨Lσ_i, Lσ_j⟩)_{i,j<m}·G(A).
5. (Basis invariance.) By steps 2 and 3, span σ = S = Q(ψ(v)). Apply the sibling gram_basis_invariance with Q := Q(ψ(v)), L, n := m and τ := σ. With τ' := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (Q(ψ(v))) it gives det(⟨Lτ'_i, Lτ'_j⟩)_{i,j<dim Q(ψ(v))} = det(⟨Lσ_i, Lσ_j⟩)_{i,j<m}. The square root of the left side is J(ψ(v)), by definition.
6. (Conclusion.)
- By steps 1, 4 and 5, G(D(Φ∘ψ)(v)) = det(⟨L(Ae_k), L(Ae_l)⟩) = det(⟨Lσ_i, Lσ_j⟩)·G(A) = det(⟨Lτ'_i, Lτ'_j⟩)·G(A).
- G(A) > 0 by step 4, so √(x·G(A)) = √x·√G(A) for every real x (Real.sqrt_mul').
- Hence √G(D(Φ∘ψ)(v)) = √det(⟨Lτ'_i, Lτ'_j⟩)·√G(A) = J(ψ(v))·√G(Dψ(v)).
- Together with step 4, the statement is proved. (For m = 0 all Gram determinants over Fin 0 are 1 and the identities are trivial instances of the same argument.) ∎

A is injective, so range A has dimension m; reindex stdOrthonormalBasis of range A to an orthonormal frame σ : Fin m → ℝ^P spanning range A.
gram_chain gives G(A) > 0 and det(⟨LAe_k, LAe_l⟩) = det(⟨Lσ_i, Lσ_j⟩)·G(A).
gram_basis_invariance replaces σ by stdOrthonormalBasis of Q(ψ(v)), which gives J(ψ(v))². Take square roots with Real.sqrt_mul' (G(A) ≥ 0).
